goals.goal: How do I cross-compile a Rust binary for aarch64 Linux with cargo?

nuggets.text: Install the standard library for the target with `rustup target add <target>` (`rustup target list` shows available targets).
Build for the target by passing the `--target` flag to Cargo, e.g. `cargo build --target=<triple>`.
`rustup target add` only installs the Rust standard library for the target; cross-compiling typically also needs other tools, particularly a linker.
A linker for a target is configured in Cargo config with the `target.<triple>.linker` key, i.e. a `[target.<triple>]` table with `linker = "..."`.
The linker setting can also be given through the environment variable `CARGO_TARGET_<triple>_LINKER`.
aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu is a Tier 1 with Host Tools target (ARM64 Linux, kernel 4.1+, glibc 2.17+).

goals.goal: How do I squash the last 3 commits in git?

nuggets.text: Start an interactive rebase with `git rebase -i HEAD~3`.
In the rebase todo list, keep `pick` on the first (oldest) commit and change `pick` to `squash` on the other two commits.
After saving the todo list, Git opens the editor again so you can combine the three commit messages into one.
`fixup` is like `squash` but discards the commit's log message.
Rebasing rewrites the commits (changes their SHA-1s), so do not include commits you have already pushed to a shared repository.

goals.goal: How do I set a default value for a column in PostgreSQL with ALTER TABLE?

nuggets.text: Use the syntax `ALTER TABLE name ALTER [ COLUMN ] column_name SET DEFAULT expression`.
The new default value only applies to subsequent INSERT or UPDATE commands; it does not change rows already in the table.
To remove a default use `ALTER COLUMN column_name DROP DEFAULT`, which is equivalent to setting the default to NULL.
When adding a new column with `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT now()`, existing rows are filled with the default value as the value of the new column.
Multiple actions can be combined in one statement, e.g. `ALTER TABLE transactions ADD COLUMN status varchar(30) DEFAULT 'old', ALTER COLUMN status SET default 'current';`.

goals.goal: How do I pin a GitHub Action to a commit SHA in my workflow?

nuggets.text: Reference the action with its full commit SHA after the `@` in `uses:`, e.g. `uses: actions/javascript-action@a824008085750b8e136effc585c3cd6082bd575f`.
You must use a commit's full SHA value, not an abbreviated one.
Verify that the SHA comes from the action's own repository and not from a fork.
Pinning to a full-length commit SHA is currently the only way to use an action as an immutable release, whereas tags can be moved or deleted.
The tradeoff of SHA pinning is that you do not automatically receive updates, including bug fixes and security updates.
GitHub offers repository-level and organization-level policies that require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA.

goals.goal: How do I roll back a Kubernetes Deployment to a previous revision with kubectl?

nuggets.text: List the revisions with `kubectl rollout history deployment/<name>` (e.g. deployment/nginx-deployment).
Inspect a specific revision with `kubectl rollout history deployment/nginx-deployment --revision=2`.
Roll back to the previous revision with `kubectl rollout undo deployment/nginx-deployment`.
Roll back to a specific revision with `kubectl rollout undo deployment/nginx-deployment --to-revision=2`.
By default all of the Deployment's rollout history is kept in the system, and this can be changed by modifying the revision history limit.

goals.goal: How do I build only one stage of a multi-stage Dockerfile?

nuggets.text: Use `docker build --target <stage-name> -t <tag> .` to stop at a specific build stage (e.g. `docker build --target build -t hello .`).
Name a stage by adding `AS <NAME>` to its `FROM` instruction (e.g. `FROM golang:1.26 AS build`).
Copy artifacts from an earlier stage with `COPY --from=<stage>` (e.g. `COPY --from=build /bin/hello /bin/hello`).
Unnamed stages can be referenced by integer index starting at 0 for the first `FROM` instruction.
With BuildKit, only the stages that the target stage depends on are built, whereas the legacy builder processes all stages leading up to the selected target.

goals.goal: How do I make Node.js automatically restart my script when files change?

nuggets.text: Run the script with the `--watch` flag, e.g. `node --watch index.js`.
By default watch mode watches the entry point and any required or imported module.
Use `--watch-path` (e.g. `node --watch-path=./src --watch-path=./tests index.js`) to specify which paths to watch; this turns off watching of required or imported modules.
Watch mode became stable in Node.js v22.0.0 and v20.13.0 (the flag was added in v18.11.0 and v16.19.0).
`--watch` requires a file path argument and cannot be combined with `--check`, `--eval`, `--interactive`, or the REPL; if no file is provided Node.js exits with status code 9.

goals.goal: How do I create and activate a Python virtual environment with venv?

nuggets.text: Create the environment by running the venv module: `python -m venv /path/to/new/virtual/environment`.
On POSIX with bash/zsh activate it with `source <venv>/bin/activate`.
On Windows activate it with `<venv>\Scripts\activate.bat` in cmd.exe or `<venv>\Scripts\Activate.ps1` in PowerShell.
Deactivate a virtual environment by typing `deactivate` in the shell.
The `--system-site-packages` option gives the virtual environment access to the system site-packages directory.
Virtual environments are not movable or copyable and should not be checked into source control; recreate them in the target location instead (e.g. with `pip install -r requirements.txt`).
